observation.visible_scene: Nighttime fireworks display seen across a dark, calm body of water. A low horizon with scattered city/town lights sits on the left; the sky above the water's edge is filled with bright bursts whose mirror images stretch down into the water. The camera framing of the horizon and shoreline stays essentially fixed throughout.
visible_changes: At the start, two large dome-shaped bursts (pink/white/green streaks) sit at the center; over the first ~15 frames their streaks droop downward and dim as the sparks fall, while the water reflection mirrors this fade.

A thin vertical launch trail on the right side persists and, from about frame 19 onward, a row of vertical trails higher in the sky develops small palm/willow-shaped bursts (orange-white sparks) that expand outward and then fade.

From roughly frame 31 to the end, additional spherical bursts bloom in the upper-center and upper-right, expanding into colored rings/cores (blue, green, orange) that grow in diameter and brighten the sky and the reflection.

The reflection column in the water continuously tracks the sky: it shifts from the drooping central domes to the brighter, more colorful high bursts near the end, with the red glow on the left horizon intensifying around frames 22-41.
No editing cut is present; the sequence reads as one continuous stretch of an ongoing display.
Camera position relative to the horizon and left-side lights shows no clear pan or zoom; apparent small shifts are treated as minor handheld jitter rather than intentional motion.
outside_clip_unknowns: What happened before t=0 and after the last frame (earlier bursts, final fade-out).
The exact launch points and number of shells; only the visible trails and bursts are shown.
Whether the faint vertical streaks at far left are water reflections, searchlights, or trails.
uncertain_details: Sub-pixel camera stability (slight jitter vs. fixed).
Whether the red glow near the left horizon is a separate ground light or a low firework burst.

the excerpt form a complete story. Missing context outside this segment stays unknown.

do not invent a smooth transition or a causal mechanism to connect the two views.

properties. Cover the main visible process, not just scenery. Distinguish object movement from
camera movement, reflection from separate objects, expansion from translation, deformation from
occlusion, and an already ongoing process from its onset. Only state what the clip supports;

and their relative positions before describing motion. Treat camera motion as uncertain when the
background evidence is insufficient, and retain clear relative changes despite that uncertainty.
